summary.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 93.8% YoY to INR 35.85 crore and FY26 PAT grew 81.8% to INR 15.20 crore; management guides FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore plus.
summary.overview: Dachepalli Publishers reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR 35.85 crore (up 93.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5.79 crore (16.2% margin) and PAT of INR 5.16 crore (14.4% margin). For FY26, total income was INR 91.39 crore (up 42.2%), EBITDA INR 23.52 crore (25.7% margin, up 524 bps) and PAT INR 15.20 crore (16.6% margin, up 362 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to lower paper prices, bulk production under a common national curriculum, and free technology bundled into textbook pricing. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore-plus (internal stretch INR 160-165 crore) and PAT margin of 16-17%, with an INR 220-230 crore target for FY28.

segments.name: Textbooks (CBSE, ICSE, State boards)
segments.commentary: Supplied to about 10,000 schools in 15 states; management says market share in the 10 original states rose from about 1% to 2%, and four new states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Assam) were added. FY27 textbook target is about INR 90 crore.

segments.name: E-commerce (Pelican Edu Supply)
segments.commentary: About 50 schools generated approx. INR 20 crore in FY26; management targets 150 schools and INR 50-60 crore in FY27 across textbooks, notebooks, stationery and uniforms. Management says 50% textbook purchase is a condition for participating schools.

segments.name: Notebooks and stationery
segments.commentary: Notebook manufacturing machinery is being commissioned (about 10 tonnes/day capacity, 80% already ordered per management). Stationery volume with e-commerce schools is about 8,000-9,000 units; management says in-house stationery needs about 30,000 units.

segments.name: Uniforms
segments.commentary: Piloted at 3 schools in FY26; FY27 rollout limited to the 50 existing e-commerce schools. Management cited EBITDA margins close to 50% on uniforms, which it described as preliminary.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: INR 150 crore-plus as the minimum; management estimates INR 160-165 crore internally.
FY27 PAT margin of 16-17%, which management uses as the basis for EBITDA estimates.
FY27 PAT estimate of around INR 25 crore (stated on the call).
FY28 revenue target of INR 200-250 crore, with INR 220-230 crore described as achievable.
Long term: more than INR 500 crore turnover in 5-6 years (CEO's stated target); entry into all 28 states and 8 UTs within 3 years.
No dividend in FY26; may consider dividend next year after reaching internal targets.
capex_capacity: Printing capacity about 15 tonnes/day, utilisation about 75% vs about 40% earlier; about 85% of production in-house. Management says it can support about INR 250 crore turnover with added ancillary machinery (about INR 3 crore) and a second shift.
Notebook manufacturing machinery acquired in FY26; management expects full operation by 30 June 2026. Capacity about 10 tonnes/day per management.
Company-owned warehouse of about 1,50,000 sq ft, which management says can handle up to INR 300 crore turnover.
Management says no major capex planned for the next 3-4 years except the notebook machine; beyond INR 200-300 crore, more machinery and working capital may be needed.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the FY26 margin expansion to a fall in paper prices (INR 120/kg in 2020 vs INR 65/kg last year, per management) and to one national curriculum under NEP 2020, which lowered plate and print-run costs.
Free technology bundled with textbooks lifted textbook MRP by about INR 10 (from INR 150 to INR 160-170 per management); management says this helped drive adoption.
Seasonality: management said about 80% of business falls in Q4 and Q1 and about 20% in Q2 and Q3, with off-academic products such as worksheets sold in those quarters.
Competitors named: Navneet Education, S. Chand and Chetana Education.
Management said uniform EBITDA margins are close to 50%, but this is preliminary and not yet proven at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from about INR 64 crore FY25 revenue to INR 90 crore FY26, and how much was own product versus other publishers' books and notebooks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textbooks were about INR 60 crore in FY25 and about INR 70 crore in FY26, with e-commerce about INR 20 crore. Exact split of notebooks and third-party books was not provided; management said it would share later.

qa_highlights.question: Where are receivable days coming from, and is the 200-day figure a real issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said invoicing starts in October, but schools reopen on 15 June and pay only after that, so the financial cycle looks longer than the academic cycle (which it said is effectively about 90 days from June).

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 inventory high at INR 50-54 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closing stock is built by March for the June-July academic sales and cannot be avoided because schools place orders from October and publishers need stock ready by end September.

qa_highlights.question: Are EBITDA margins sustainable, and what drove the FY26 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cheaper paper (about 40-50% lower), one national curriculum that cut plate and print-run costs, and free technology that lifted sales volume. It guided PAT margin of 16-17% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much does Pelican Edu Supply contribute and is it profitable without cash burn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the platform is profitable and built in-house with no cash burn. About INR 20 crore came from 50 schools in FY26, and about INR 50-60 crore is expected from 150 schools in FY27. Parents pay shipping separately.

qa_highlights.question: How can revenue reach INR 250 crore on the current 15 tonne/day printing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ancillary machines run below capacity; about INR 3 crore of extra machinery on the existing line and a second shift could support INR 200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from Maharashtra's rule letting students buy textbooks and uniforms from anywhere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such rules are typically announced before reopening; it argued parents prefer one-stop baskets and that its own bundled e-commerce model addresses that.

risks_watch: Receivable days (about 200 per the analyst, though management argues it is an academic-cycle effect) and inventory build of INR 50-54 crore at 31 March 2026.
Execution of the 150-school e-commerce rollout and uniform scale-up, from a base of 50 schools and 3 pilot schools; the uniform margin of about 50% is not yet proven.
State-level regulation (Maharashtra) allowing students to buy textbooks and uniforms from any vendor, which could weaken school-linked bundling.
Management's FY27 guidance has a large step-up from FY26; management's stated ratio of 16-17% PAT margin needs to hold while scaling sales and marketing headcount in new states.
Notebook machinery commissioning by 30 June 2026 and whether in-house notebooks replace third-party purchases as stated.
Paper price volatility, since management said paper is about 70% of textbook product cost.
Analyst questions on whether the company makes margin on the third-party textbooks and stationery, and the data on notebook revenue, were not fully answered.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and targets, with multiple forward figures given without a clear basis. Vague or deflective on the bridge of revenue split, the working capital metrics and the drivers of margin expansion, which it attributed to several factors without quantifying each.
